worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosine function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (6{x}^{2}-\frac{3}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}})\text{d}x & =6\int {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{x}^{3}-3\operatorname{arcosh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
